jurisdiction.name: Ghana
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Ghana governs AI through its National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025-2035, launched in April 2026, which proposes a Responsible AI Authority, and through the Data Protection Act 2012, which regulates decisions based solely on automated processing. Two consultation drafts from 2025 would go further: a new Data Protection Bill making technology-driven decisions explainable and contestable, and an Emerging Technologies Bill creating an agency with an AI division. Neither has been enacted.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents read in full on official sites. The ministry's news pages could not be accessed, so a March 2026 announcement on responsible AI adoption could not be read. The Responsible AI Authority, the national AI delivery roadmap and the health ministry's AI policy are tracked as leads. As a large country with few records, Ghana is marked for a longer catch-up pass.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations
instruments.current_status: Cover dated December 2025; officially launched on 24 April 2026 in Accra (Minister's launch remarks, which refer to its approval and launch). A separate 104-page appendices volume is published on moc.gov.gh (https://moc.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/National-AI-Strategy-Appendices.pdf). Next steps named at the launch: a National AI Delivery Roadmap and an Emerging Technologies Bill (see leads). An earlier 'National AI Strategy 2023-2033' listed by international trackers was not found as an official government publication.
instruments.summary: Ghana's first official national AI strategy, a ten-year roadmap ('Ghana 2035: The AI-Powered Society') built on the Digital Economy Policy and Strategy and the Ghana Integrated Digital Transformation Blueprint. It sets an action plan under eight pillars (AI education, youth and jobs, digital infrastructure, data access and governance, the AI ecosystem, sector adoption, applied research and public-sector adoption), including reviewing intellectual-property law and calling for AI sandboxing environments. It recommends establishing an independent Responsible AI Authority in the first year, incubated by the Data Protection Commission, to coordinate implementation and lead quarterly monitoring.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main national AI policy document; proposes the national AI governance body (Responsible AI Authority).

instruments.summary: National digital economy policy of the Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation setting strategies for infrastructure, digital skills, data and emerging technologies. Its section 'Special Emphasis on Artificial Intelligence' treats AI as an emerging technology with both opportunity and risk, positions the policy's data governance measures as baseline guardrails for AI, cites Ghana's adoption of the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, and recommends steps (awareness, responsible experimentation) towards a comprehensive national AI strategy.

instruments.current_status: In force; assented to 10 May 2012 and notified in the Gazette on 18 May 2012. The commencement date is not stated in the Act text read (effective_date left null). A Data Protection Bill, 2025 that would repeal and replace it was published in draft for consultation by the Ministry in October 2025 (separate record).
instruments.summary: Ghana's general data protection law, which establishes the Data Protection Commission and regulates the obtaining, holding, use and disclosure of personal data, with registration duties for data controllers. Section 41 gives individuals the right to require that decisions significantly affecting them are not based solely on automatic processing of their personal data, and obliges controllers to notify individuals of such decisions and reconsider them on request within 21 days, with exceptions for contracts and decisions authorised by law.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data protection law governing personal data used in AI systems, with rights on solely automated decisions (s.41).

instruments.summary: Draft bill to replace the Data Protection Act, 2012 by establishing a Data Protection Authority and updating data subject rights. Clause 53 ('Application of Emerging Technologies') requires technology-driven decisions affecting data subjects to be explainable, contestable and subject to human oversight, and empowers the Authority to regulate such processing and conduct risk assessments; clause 65 adds a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions including profiling, listing chatbots, 'emerging technology systems' and facial and emotional recognition as automated processing. 'Emerging technologies' is defined to include artificial intelligence.

instruments.summary: Draft bill to establish an Emerging Technologies Agency, with an Artificial Intelligence Division among others, to promote and facilitate the adoption of emerging technologies and provide harmonised rules on their obligations, rights, ethics and safety. It sets guiding principles for emerging technology systems covering democratic integrity, non-discrimination and bias, transparency and oversight, personal data protection, accountability, reliability, risk and impact management (identification and mitigation of risks to human rights, democracy and the rule of law), human oversight, misinformation, security and a right to redress, with enforcement and regulation-making powers.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Draft AI framework law; would create the national body overseeing AI and other emerging technologies.

Draft bills dated '2025' (uploads 20-21 Oct 2025). Act 843 commencement (16 Oct 2012 per DPC guidance) not read; effective_date null. Ghana AI Practitioners' Guide (Sep 2025) hosted only by GIZ/BMZ: not recorded. No official text of 'National AI Strategy 2023-2033'. Convention 108 act not found. Units covered: Law: Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843) read in full; Cybersecurity Act 2020 has no AI provisions found (not recorded). No enacted AI law; Emerging Technologies Bill 2025 and Data Protection Bill 2025 consultation drafts read (moc.gov.gh). Parliament site not searched directly (bills not yet laid per ministry statements).; Government: MoCDTI: National AI Strategy 2025-2035 (+appendices, launch remarks) and Digital Economy Policy and Strategy 2024 read. No public-sector AI guideline, procurement rule, transparency register, standard or government readiness index found on moc.gov.gh.; Ministries: Health: AI Health Policy under development (lead). Education/GES, justice, defence, finance, labour, interior: searched, nothing found.; Regulators: Data Protection Commission: Act 843 and general compliance guidelines only, no AI guidance. Cyber Security Authority, Bank of Ghana, SEC, NCA: searched, no AI-specific documents found.. Not reached: moc.gov.gh news pages (launch article 2026-04-24, 'Ghana Paves Way for Responsible AI Adoption' 2026-03-06) timed out: curl reset and WebFetch 503; parliament.gh order papers not searched directly; bog.gov.gh / sec.gov.gh / nca.org.gh / csa.gov.gh own site searches not run (discovery search only).
